body.en:
Question B-004-001-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Speech audio in a transceiver is processed over the voice range used for communications audio: 300 Hz to 3 000 Hz.

Choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "300 Hz to 3 000 Hz": This range covers the main voice frequencies normally passed by a communications speech amplifier. Numeric check: the lower edge is 300 Hz and the upper edge is 3 000 Hz.
- sourceIndex 1: "3 Hz to 300 Hz": This is mostly very low audio and would exclude much of intelligible speech. Numeric check: 3 Hz is below the useful voice passband and 300 Hz is only the lower edge.
- sourceIndex 2: "300 Hz to 1 000 Hz": This stops too low for normal communications speech clarity. Numeric check: 1 000 Hz is far below the usual upper speech-audio edge in this context.
- sourceIndex 3: "40 Hz to 40 000 Hz": This is a broad high-fidelity audio range, not the narrower communications speech passband. Numeric check: 40 000 Hz is well beyond voice communications audio.
